top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu, B014) is the only proposal on the slate and the only one that names a writer. It is a single-writer, single-prize-part configuration with unambiguous attribution. On the common criteria, his voice is distinctive. The Blinding trilogy and Solenoid are conceived as large, patterned structures in which memory, the body and dream form one project rather than a list of themes. The architecture is visible even through translation, so the case does not rest only on reputation. The poetic origin of the prose supports reading the work as an arc across a whole oeuvre, not a single peak. I give no weight to the six-way convergence as merit. My reservations remain: I judge Romanian sentence rhythm and density only through translations of uneven quality, I cannot confirm volume by volume that the later books extend the project rather than restate it, and the poetry and early work are the thinnest part of my evidence. The 'grounded in poetry' clause is therefore the least secure part of my citation. Nothing in round 2 substantiated repetition or showed the poetry to be minor, and the citation can be narrowed to what the committee can assess. P000 ranks second because those unresolved uncertainties are not strong enough to justify no award. I have not independently verified any source.
